content: CLUAP1, also referred to as Clusterin-associated protein 1, is a gene found in humans. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the functional role of CLUAP1. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Cluap1tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was developed as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis initiative aimed at creating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers worldwide. Both male and female mice from this knockout line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the consequences of gene deletion. A total of 26 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and four significant abnormalities were identified. Notably, no homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, and as a result, none survived to the weaning stage. The remaining tests were performed on heterozygous mutant adult mice. In these mice, both males and females exhibited reduced levels of IgG1. Additionally, male mice demonstrated abnormal spinal curvature, which manifested as kyphosis.
